exposure: advanced maternal age (40 years or older)
outcome: frequency of cesarean delivery by Robson classification
cohort: The study included 47,654 women aged 20 or older delivering babies with gestational age > 28 weeks and birth weight > 1000g in Dongguan People's Hospital, China, between 2017 and 2020.
finding: The cesarean section rates increased noticeably with maternal age, with women aged 40 or older being three times more likely to undergo a cesarean delivery in Robson group 1' and 1.76 times more likely in group 10.
mod_finding: The total CS rate was 40.64%, significantly increasing with maternal age, from 36.10% for mothers aged 20-34 to 64.75% for those aged 40 or older.
